html:
This is the British Columbia part of the lands of the Carcross/Tagish First Nation, south of the Yukon border around Atlin and Tagish lakes. The nation's centre is Carcross in the Yukon; see Carcross/Tagish First Nation (Yukon).

Its people are Tagish and Inland Tlingit. The Tagish once spoke an Athabaskan language but took up Tlingit through trade and marriage with the coast. In 1896 two Tagish men, Skookum Jim and Dawson Charlie, with Kate Carmack and George Carmack, found the gold that started the Klondike Gold Rush. Thousands of gold seekers then crossed the Chilkoot Pass and passed through these lakes. Their neighbours include the Teslin Tlingit.
